summary: A worker-placement game where you gather resources to construct grand buildings for the King while deciding whether to play virtuously or dabble in smuggling and sabotage. Other players can throw your workers in jail or steal your resources, which keeps everyone glancing sideways at the shared building sites and the black market.
praised: tight worker-placement puzzle with meaningful choices
virtue/corruption track adds a moral dimension to strategy
good player interaction without full-on chaos
criticised: can feel mean when workers get jailed repeatedly
some rules overhead (raiding, contracts) for newer players
downtime between turns in higher player counts

interaction.kind: locking/jailing opponents' workers and stealing their goods
interaction.detail: Players place workers on largely separate action spots to gather resources and build contracts, but Virtue/Vice cards let you imprison a rival's worker, rob their stockpile, or block their building progress. Most of a turn is still spent developing your own contracts and buildings; the take-that cards are a periodic, targeted disruption rather than a constant fight over shared space.
interaction.said: Often called one of the more aggressive worker-placement games — reviewers note you can jail an opponent's worker, steal their goods via the Black Market, or torch their progress with Warrant cards, more "take-that" than typical Euro worker placement

scoring.how_you_win: Spend resources and workers to construct buildings and contribute to the Cathedral while managing your Virtue reputation and debts; once the Guildhall's worker supply runs out, everyone finishes the round and all VP sources are totaled, with the highest sum winning.
